newsitem.title: FRANCE: Star French judge takes over Dickinson murder probe.
newsitem.headline: Star French judge takes over Dickinson murder probe.

text.p: A French court on Thursday ordered a star magistrate to take over a year-old inquiry into the unsolved rape-murder of British teenager Caroline Dickinson in western France, justice sources said.
The appeals court in Rennes removed Gerard Zaug from the case and entrusted it to Judge Renaud van Ruymbeke, one of the country's best-known investigating jurists.

The court also ordered police to carry out systematic genetics tests on all men aged 15 to 35 in Pleine-Fougeres, the Brittany village where the 13-year-old girl was strangled on July 18, 1996 while on a school trip from Launceston, England.
She was attacked by an unidentified man in her dormitory while other girls slept nearby.

Van Ruymbeke, who has gained a reputation for tenacity in his investigations of political sleaze scandals, was due to meet investigators of the paramilitary gendarmerie later in the day to discuss the case.
"We are very happy with what happened today. New avenues will be explored," Caroline's father told reporters.
He said van Ruymbeke told him during a one-hour meeting that new methods of investigation would be used since traditional methods had failed.
The Dickinsons had sought to have Zaug and the gendarmerie taken off the case, arguing that they had made several mistakes.

They filed a fresh lawsuit last month to demand further investigations, with a formal application for wider genetic testing, a public appeal for witnesses and the linking of the investigation with another probe into a sexual attack at a youth hostel a few km (miles) away on the same night.
A few hours before Caroline's murder, a man had broken into a hostel in Saint-Lunaire, where another British school group was staying, but fled before he could be identified.

French gendarmes have conducted about 250 genetic tests in the last year on the staff and residents of the youth hostel, the schoolchidren in Caroline's group and other suspects detained in sex offence cases.
Police arrested a homeless local man a few days after the murder of Caroline, but released him after he retracted a confession and DNA tests ruled him out as a suspect.
